settings.heading: the problem no one was talking about.
settings.body:
The Kamasutra was never just about sex positions. It was a science of relationships. A guide to understanding our own desires, your partner's body, and the art of being fully present.

Our ancestors built that knowledge deliberately, and treated it with reverence. We live in its birthplace and know almost none of it.

The result is chronic dissatisfaction: partners feeling disconnected, people carrying shame around their own pleasure, and an entire conversation that never happens.
settings.pull_quote: We live in its birthplace and know almost none of it. This is the problem we were built to solve.

settings.quote: Our ancestors had answers. We're just translating them.

settings.heading: why ancient wisdom.
settings.body:
We didn't need to import a framework for sex. Intimacy wasn't always reduced to technique or outcome. There was a time when it was understood as something deeper, something to be explored, not rushed.

Our own tradition, which saw sex as science, poetry, and self-knowledge, was quietly buried. The Kamasutra was not lost. It was colonised out of our consciousness.

Pillowta exists to bring it back. Not as a museum exhibit, but as living, practical wisdom for the problems of modern intimacy.

settings.title: Living, Not Museum
settings.text: We're not preserving history. We're translating it into something you can use today.

settings.title: Science of Relationships
settings.text: The Kamasutra codified desire, presence, and mutual understanding centuries before modern psychology existed.

settings.quote: Our ancestors had answers. We're just translating them.

settings.heading: We inherited extraordinary. And forgot it.
settings.intro: India gave the world the Kamasutra. A philosophy of desire, presence, and intimacy as art. Somewhere along the way, we decided to be ashamed of it. Our ancestors built that knowledge deliberately, and treated it with reverence.
